title: Q1. Print Balanced Parentheses
statement:
Given n pairs of parentheses (so n=3 produces arrangements such as ((())), not n=6), print every balanced arrangement using exactly n opening and n closing parentheses. Print one arrangement per line; any order is accepted.

Input: n, the number of pairs. Output: all balanced arrangements, one per line.

title: Q2. Print Ways to Climb n Steps
statement:
You can climb either 1 or 2 steps at a time. Print every sequence of steps that reaches exactly n steps, one sequence per line. Separate numbers by spaces; any order is accepted.

Input: n. Output: all valid sequences.

title: Q3. Josephus Survivor
statement:
n people stand in a circle, numbered 1 to n. Starting from person 1, eliminate every k-th remaining person until one survivor remains. Print the survivor's position (1-indexed).

Input: n k.

title: Q4. Bank Account Hacks
statement:
You start with 1 rupee. A hack may multiply your amount by 10 or by 20. Each hack can be used any number of times. Print Yes if exactly N rupees can be reached, otherwise print No.

Input: N.

title: Q5. Find a Path in a Maze
statement: Given an N x N grid where 1 is open and 0 is blocked, start at (0,0) and reach (N-1,N-1). You may move up, down, left, or right. Print Yes if a path exists, otherwise No.

title: Q8. All Binary Strings of Length n
statement: Print all binary strings of length n, one per line. Any order is accepted.

title: Q1. Bubble Sort with a Function Pointer
statement:
Read an array of integers and sort it using Bubble Sort. Use a function pointer to choose the sorting order: option 1 means ascending and option 2 means descending. The function pointer must decide whether two adjacent elements need to be swapped. Use pointer parameters for the swap operation.

Pointer requirement: Solve this question using pointers only.

Input: N, followed by N integers, followed by O.
Output: the sorted array on one line, with elements separated by spaces.

title: Q2. Collatz Steps Through a Pointer
statement:
Take a positive integer n. Repeatedly apply the Collatz rule: if n is even, replace it with n / 2; otherwise replace it with 3*n + 1. Print the number of steps needed to reach 1. Implement the update through a pointer to n, and use a recursive function to count the steps.

Pointer requirement: Solve this question using pointers only.

Input: one positive integer n.
Output: the number of steps to reach 1.

title: Q3. Container With Most Water Using Two Pointers
statement:
Given heights of n vertical lines, find the maximum amount of water that can be stored between any two lines and the x-axis. The area between positions left and right is min(height[left], height[right]) * (right - left). Use two integer pointers, one at each end of the array, and move the pointer at the shorter line inward. Do not use nested loops or array indexing for the search.

Pointer requirement: Solve this question using pointers only.

Input: n followed by n non-negative heights.
Output: the maximum area. If n is less than 2, output 0.

title: Q4. Greedy Pilgrimage Path with a Matrix Pointer
statement:
Given an M x N grid of positive or negative spiritual significance values, start at the top-left cell and reach the bottom-right cell by moving only right or down. At each step, if both moves are available, choose the neighboring cell with the larger value; move right when the values are equal. Add every visited value to the total and print the total followed by the path values. Store the matrix in one dynamically allocated flat array and access cells through pointer arithmetic; do not use a variable-length 2D array or matrix indexing.

Pointer requirement: Solve this question using pointers only.

Input: M and N followed by the grid.
Output: the total on the first line and the visited values on the second line.
